description: Struck off charge at Amberley in July 1973 and sent to RSTT Wagga as a training aid, then displayed at the front gate. Externally refurbished in May 2011 and on display at the heritage centre.
To RSTT Wagga in June 1958 as instructional airframe No.5; required for display purposes from December 1961 and still held at Wagga in 1988. On display at RAAF Forest Hill.
Damaged by an engine bay fire at Nowra in April 1976, rebuilt using parts from A3-8 and sent to RSTT Wagga as a training aid. On display on the gate at RAAF Forest Hill.
aliases: Mirage IIIO; Mirage; Dassault Mirage III

description: Logged 4181.2 hours and 5027 landings before retirement in June 1987. Formerly displayed at the RAAF Museum Point Cook; transported by road to RAAF Wagga, arriving 19 September 2018.
aliases: Mirage IIIO; Mirage; Dassault Mirage III

description: Departed Amberley in March 2012 but turned back because of floods; finally left on 12 June 2012 and arrived at Wagga Wagga on 14 June 2012. On display in an enclosure at the gate of RAAF Base Wagga.

First flew 27 June 1967; served with the Central Flying School in the Telstars aerobatic team 1967-70, then 2FTS and 76 Squadron. To RSTT Wagga in November 2000 as a training aid and displayed as the RAAF Wagga gate guard from November 2018.

The CA-22 Winjeel prototype. Instructional airframe at RSTT Wagga, then the RAAF Museum from 1983 and on display at the Fleet Air Arm Museum Nowra; relocated to the RAAF Base Wagga Aviation Heritage Centre in 2020.
A Jindivik marked A92-511 is mounted on a pole outside the Airmen Club at RAAF Base Wagga Wagga.
Central Flying School Telstars 1968-70, then 2FTS, the Roulettes and 76 Squadron. Held as a training aid at the RAAF School of Technical Training, Wagga Wagga.
Carried the 76 Squadron commemorative scheme; served with 76 Squadron from May 1999 and used as a training aid at the RAAF School of Technical Training, Wagga Wagga.
